records.note: The deadline is clean ('in 10 years' = 2033-04-10) and the asset is clean (neuromodulation), but 'almost all psychiatric conditions' is a quantifier with no countable set and no threshold. The registry already holds the bounded version of the same claim (E-0013, neuromodulation first-line for MDD). A broader entry could only be written by inventing a share of the diagnoses, so test (f) fails.

event.asset: A permanent DEA rule for telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances
event.title: DEA adopts a permanent rule for telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances
event.proposition: The DEA adopts a permanent rule that governs the prescribing of controlled substances by telemedicine.
event.criterion: TRUE on the Federal Register publication date of a DEA final rule that sets a permanent framework for prescribing controlled substances by telemedicine without a prior in-person medical evaluation. A proposed rule, a temporary rule, and a further extension of the COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities are not adoption. FALSE at the deadline when no such final rule has been published. Resolution source: the Federal Register.
readings: 'They' = the DEA, per the immediate context.
'Figure it out' = adopt a permanent telemedicine prescribing rule, per the immediate context; a further temporary extension does not count.
Distinct from the entry on the February 2023 proposed rule being revised, withdrawn or replaced (E-0012) and from the entry on the per-state physical-location registration requirement (E-0007).

records.stage_note: DEA telemedicine rulemaking pending on the statement date; the dea_telemedicine_extension class covers a further extension, not a permanent rule, so no class fits.
records.note: The deciding body (DEA) and the act (a permanent telemedicine prescribing rule) come from the immediate context, and the Federal Register resolves it. 'Eventually' is not a deadline, so the item goes to the undated panel. 'They'll' sets bin A.

Not CONTROL: the author's clinic cannot make a modality the standard of care. The defect is scope and benchmark. 'Standard of care' names no resolution source, and the subject is an open list that ends in 'other novel interventions', so the set is unbounded. 'In the near future' is not a deadline either.

The headline claim, 'more effective treatment coming', is a quantifier with no countable set and no deadline ('coming', 'in the future'). The four named candidates are listed as pipeline examples with four different hedges, and the author closes with 'I don't actually know'. No single observable event can be written.

event.title: UnitedHealthcare covers accelerated TMS for depression

records.phrase: United ain't budging any time soon
records.stage_note: UnitedHealthcare does not cover accelerated TMS for humans on the statement date; no external class covers a payer coverage change.
records.note: Coded on the United clause: a flat denial that UnitedHealthcare changes its accelerated-TMS coverage stance for humans, so bin A with asserts false. 'Any time soon' is not a deadline. The private-equity and veterinary clause names no deciding body and no countable set, and E-0040 excludes veterinary coverage, so it is not written into the event. Affiliated is false: the forecaster holds no role in UnitedHealthcare, the only entity in the event.

'Might work' for adolescent depression is an efficacy opinion with no trial, no endpoint, no regulator and no deadline. The paired sentence, 'We should run the studies', is normative. No observable event can be written without inventing a trial.
A presupposition inside a clause about financials. It names no drug, no device, no regulator and no threshold, and 'are coming' is not a deadline. Nothing beyond a class word can be written.

The main verb is retrospective: Spravato 'has already been approved'. The rest, 'can be successfully overcome', states a capability drawn from that past approval, not an expectation that a named body acts by a date. Test (d) fails: information, not expectation. The forecast from this post is already in the ledger as the separate 'strong chance that MDMA will get approved' line.

Two halves, neither admissible. The re-domiciliation is his own company's completed action. '2026 will be a defining year for $ATAI' is a slogan with no observable event and no threshold. He states that a prerequisite is met; he never states that index inclusion happens, so E-0059 could only be written by inventing the claim.

'FDA guidance has been consistent' describes guidance already in force on the statement date. No future state is asserted and no deciding body is said to act. Reading it as a denial of retail-pharmacy dispensing (E-0067) would add a future approval the forecaster did not name.

The forward-looking content is attributed, not adopted: 'what the market anticipates will be the first regulatory approval'. His own main verb, 'public sentiment has gone from ... to ...', is descriptive. Near-identical text is already logged as angermayer-0161 from the Substack post of 2026-04-20, but DUPLICATE tests the same post, so the attribution is the operative defect.

The sentence states the content of a filing his own organization has already made: 'the REMS that we have proposed preliminary with the FDA is that ...'. MAPS decided that proposal by itself, and 'preliminary' marks it as unsettled. He does not state that the FDA adopts it, so E-0077 would need an assertion he did not make. The ledger already holds his forward-tense versions of the same restriction.

The only forecast is timing: 'we're going to know before the end of September'. MAPS is the sponsor, and MAPS sets when the last data point closes, when it unblinds and when it reports. He does not say the endpoint is met, so E-0002 is not asserted. The '90% or greater probability of statistical significance' is the power at 100 participants, which he then says they cut to 90; it is a design fact, not a stated probability.

Same shape as doblin-0252: 'about a month away from having the data' forecasts when his own organization holds its own trial data. No third party decides that timing, and he states no result. 'About a month away' would anchor to 2020-11-22, but the item fails test (c) before the deadline rule applies.
